steps.text: 11:00 A.M., Somewhere in the countryside

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: We have entered Area 10 according to plan. Enemy presence sighted at three o'clock.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: How many left?

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: ...Scan complete. Three within visible range.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: There were four who fled for Area 10 just now. If we wipe out the opposing forces here, we can prevent the other side from returning combat intelligence. It'll give us an incredible advantage for our second assault.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: These three... we can't let them go, and we need to find the fourth too.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I'll go pin them down! The rest of you, just stick to the plan!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Stick to... the plan? Captain Fang, what am I supposed to be doing?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (Huh? Did I forget to explain again?)

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aciddrop, you find high ground and provide cover fire, risk mitigation. Frostleaf, stay behind me, and attack as soon as we catch the enemy.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Lens, keep tabs on the full field of view, and you have to ensure Scene's safety.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Understood. Currently verifying Lens composite camouflage defense and concealment status.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Huh? There's a burnt smell...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: ...It's an ambush from the fourth target! Sure enough, they weren't just retreating, they wanted to trick us into falling for their trap.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aciddrop, it's up to you!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Wha? So you want me igniting the ambush?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: It's set to my left. You deal with the trap, Frostleaf and I will go catch the leftovers—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Got it. Check this.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Wait up... Captain Fang, target's out of my attack range. I'm switching positions—

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (Ah, Aciddrop's specialty is high-precision, close-range fire. Her position there was too far for her fire to reach.)

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (I just planned around Kroos's attack patterns out of habit...)

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Captain Fang, Target 4... Target 4 is not ahead, they are behind—

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: It's an ambush! Captain!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Dammit, that's how they're countering Aciddrop—

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*... What the—

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Aciddrop, Aciddrop, please respond. Your signal has been interrupted—

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: I'll go look for her.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Okay, Frostleaf. You assist Aciddrop, and withdraw from the trap position. I'll find the fourth guy... I can't let anyone get away.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aciddrop, can you hear me? Aciddrop!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Captain Fang... I'm alright, the explosion just rocked my comms. *cough*...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I've found you... scoundrel!
Urghh!!

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Found her. Captain, Aciddrop is hurt.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: It's light injuries, no big. They'll be fine once I'm on the move. Relax, Captain Fang, I'm still good to fight.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Captain?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We can retreat for now. Lens, any other risks on the map?

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Area 10 is now fully secured. Further, no sign of danger on evacuation route.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Hold on, I'm alright. Captain Fang, there's still the three guys from...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: All four have been dealt with. Our mission is already complete. Area 10 is secured.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Let's pull out for the time being.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: ...Sorry.
Ten minutes later...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aciddrop... your wounds...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I'm chill... *cough*, I'm seriously alright, Captain Fang! My board covered me from pretty much most of the explosion damage, I just kinda fell and got a scrape or two.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I'm sorry... I can't believe I'm the reason you got hurt.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I should've obviously just kept up the search-and-destroy in Area 10, and we would've safely and promptly withdrawn in the end. It's all my fault...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Captain...? I'm being serious, I'm fine. See? For real, it's only a few scrapes. I'm cool for the next phase of the mission, I'm at like 90% here!

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: The other squads should be rendezvousing very soon.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Our mission's first phase is complete either way. Now we just wait to converge and carry out the next wave of our formal assault.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I was too reckless... I clearly should've known that area had a high risk of being trapped, and yet I was the first to charge in.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Your judgment wasn't at all flawed, Captain. We were just slightly disjointed in that last mission, but we didn't lose any opportunity to carry out our search-and-destroy.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Though it might seem extreme in hindsight, if we'd all gone on the offense together, we probably had sufficient strength to defeat them.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Honestly, it's not like I don't get how you were thinking either, Captain.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I could see the situation up from where I was stood just then.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Like, you've found their weakness already, Captain. You wanna rush the enemy directly, yeah? If we've got rear support watching for traps, we'll be good.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: It was a lapse in judgment with my command. I subconsciously... took my team members' combat styles to be those under simulated circumstances I knew better.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I had forgotten everyone's personal strengths by the time the mission started, and employed my habitual line of thought. I took it for granted and gave you the wrong assignment, Aciddrop.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Not just that, I even failed to clearly relay the plan to my team members... and caused everyone to spend even more energy on the mission.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I don't think you messed up at all just now, Captain. With the whole situation, putting me in charge of clearing the traps, and you and Frostleaf pursuing the enemy, that's solid tactics.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Just didn't predict the enemy would still be on the counter after that. They really bit off way more than they could chew. I mean, you dealt with them all yourself.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Miss Scene wishes to say that actually, Captain Fang truly trusts her team, and therefore believes they will understand her instructions via action?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Every captain's style of execution has its own differences. You have your own strong points, Captain Fang.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I'm kinda curious, though. You said you messed up by using a simulation you were used to? What exactly was that?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: It's... my habits with the Reserve Op Team A1, more or less. I know I'm not in any of the team's simulation exercises, but in an actual, crucial combat situation...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aaagh, what am I even doing?!

steps.name: Scene
steps.text: D o n ' t . . .

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Calm down, calm down, Captain Fang. Miss Scene is very concerned you're blaming yourself too much.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Chill out, Captain. Mission one's basically a clean finish. Get your mood out, shake yourself off, yeah? Or, uh, if you're torn-up, you can just say. We're a team right now, y'know.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: The A1 detachment, huh... your team's a real party, right? You train together, you do simmed battles together. I bet your team coordination level's through the roof.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Thank you, Aciddrop, Scene, Frostleaf... and Lens, too.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: In all honesty... I believe that when it comes to team operability, A1 doesn't fall short against other reserve detachments.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We've known each other for a very long time, and we've all reached the point we can fully understand each other's reasoning and operation methods. Some things we can get done even without words.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: That's so neat. I see you hanging with Beagle and Kroos all the time, too. You're really good friends too?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Yes... Before Beagle, Kroos and I came to Rhodes Island, we were an intern team at a Columbian garrison.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: That's some major force. All I ever had on the brain was skateboarding, back in Columbia. Only realized after hitting Rhodes Island, hey, when that old police guy taught me those crossbow techs? Actually got a use for those.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: If it was a competition, I'd be way below your league, Fang.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Even so, now you've adapted just fine to field combat missions, Aciddrop.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Heheh, you think so? It's not my first time getting a combat scrape, though. Always easy to lose track and get hurt, and I get my captains keyed up all the time with it.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: You'll improve with experience.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: A1's been through a lot of combat training.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: With how we've worked each other out, we've devised a set of handy signals only we understand.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: They give me the time and space to judge a situation. That gives me the opportunity to command as a captain. But...

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: But?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: To tell the truth, this is my first time directing combat as an official acting team leader...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I don't know why I've been unable to adjust my plans or instructions... I haven't just failed to make my orders understood, I've given the wrong orders to the wrong teammates.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I... just can't figure it out. Apart from my own incompetence, where else could the problem lie?

steps.name: Scene
steps.text: I t ' s   n o t . . .

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: You can't let yourself think that way, Captain Fang! Your response and judgment just now were completely correct.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Scene and I observed very clearly in our previous battle that your assessment of the situation was abundantly exact.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: You possessed the ability to rapidly locate the enemy's vital points on the front line, and were exceptionally brave in leading your charge to open the way for us.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: If it's just a question of bravery, it doesn't matter who, anyone on this battlefield could...

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: It doesn't stop at bravery.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Frostleaf...?

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Some people are soldiers from birth. Soldiers obedient to command.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Able to consider, assess and change their approach based on the battlefield situation, but absolutely compliant to their superiors' orders.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: But Fang, you're not just a soldier. You also have the heart to direct us.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Is that really true...? I can really do that?

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Mmhm. At least, to the best of your ability, you've enabled our team to complete this first mission.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: And besides, the way you lead A1 to victory out there in battle, and then come back and have such a great, friendly relationship, that all shows what a great captain you are.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: I mean, it's not like everyone's lucky enough to get set up in an reserve op team. Like me, I'm such a free spirit they won't even give me the chance.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: So buck up, Captain Fang.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Nobody thinks you gave the wrong orders. You're just hung up on doing better.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: If you would like to change, then learn from your failures. You definitely have what it takes to find a solution.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huff... puff...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I got it.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I'll keep working hard to be a good captain, but I hope you will all keep giving me suggestions on how to improve.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Well... Like, I guess I didn't really get why you went rushing on ahead, and it sorta freaked me out?

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Aciddrop, I think what you are trying to say is the captain should 'improve communication.'

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Yeah, that!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Right... so I need to give clear and concise commands...

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Yes, communication is important. You act and react decisively, but it's important to make sure everyone can keep up.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Get a plan in place and keep everyone safe...

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Battlefield command is very difficult, but crucial. There is no doubt you have what it takes to be captain.

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: But we hope you will provide more encouragement to your teammates, such that they will have even more faith in you.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Yeah, like, beyond just training, you and the A1 girls do other stuff to build teamwork, right?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Hm... we do talk strategy, I guess. And we fight, and chat, and argue...

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: You argue? That sounds like a rather intense pastime.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Yes, like at times like these, they'll be so caught up in themselves, I have to push them to rest, or they'll talk right through their break time...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We have thirty minutes until the next mission, so you should be resting up too. I'll wake you when it's time to move.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Wha? But I wanted to hear more about you and your reserve op team.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We can't keep talking, you're wounded. You need your rest. Lay down, Aciddrop.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Ugh, fine. But after the mission, you've gotta gimme some real tight war stories, okay? I'm jonesing.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: Miss Scene wants to ask if you have cheered up? She hopes that conversation was helpful to you.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Don't worry, Scene, or Lens. I just need a little alone time to think.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Yeah... good call.
Fifteen days ago, Rhodes Island Training Grounds

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: ...That's it for today.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Phew... alright.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Finally done... huff... I'm totally spent...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Kroos never misses a chance to catch a break... Why don't you take me up on my offer and have healthy meals with me?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You'll have more energy. We'll get you on a regular schedule.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: No thanks. I might be better off living like you, Hibiscus... but I think I'd rather take it easy.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Shhh! Kroos! The instructors are still here!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Alright, no joking around in front of Instructor Grace. Everybody form up and head out.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Fang, hold back a second.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Yes, Instructor!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Poor Fang. Team leaders always have to stay late.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: But Fang won't mind talking to the instructor for a while more. She's so responsible and serious. I couldn't handle more lessons, but Fang...?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: (And her tail's still flapping away. Fang really has so much energy.)

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Yeah, Fang's always worn her heart on her sleeve. Training doesn't get to her, not like us. We can't hold up in a protracted fight...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're the one who's always slacking off.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (You two...!)

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Ah! We'd better go! Bye, Instructor Grace, Captain Fang!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Sorry you had to see that, Instructor... I hope we don't come off too lazy...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Relax, you're doing fine. I asked you to stay not for Reserve Op Team A1, but for you yourself.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Correct. I've gleaned a few things from conversations with the rest of A1. There are some concerns about your leadership.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I... I don't want to make anyone worry.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Anyone can see that A1 has grown a lot. When you're done with training, we'll break out the team members for temporary practical duty with other squads.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: And you haven't been doing too badly as captain.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: But... I almost never do that kind of temporary duty alone.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Hibiscus, Kroos, and Beagle all had great temporary duty runs, and Lava gets out there on real missions, everyone can see how well she does alone.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: But me? I may be captain, but I only pull it off with my team's support.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I mean, I sometimes think it'd be fine to just keep on leading A1, as selfish as that is...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I wish A1 could stay together, but I know everyone has their own futures ahead of them. I... I know we have to move on.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Yes, well, your teammates have all talked about how you feel. They know your sense of responsibility and duty.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: And honestly, it's important for your feelings to get through to your teammates.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I've been around the block enough that I can tell you Rhodes Island's training regimen isn't just about getting your combat scores up.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Right, I know!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Instructor Dobermann always talks about how she wants Rhodes Island Operators to be strong and steadfast in battle, but also... to never blind themselves to the cruelty of war, to keep a beating heart.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Never see yourself as a pawn on the board.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: What that means, Fang, is a lot more opportunities for you, not only for Rhodes Island to trust in your strength, but to refresh yourself.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Re...fresh myself?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Your A1 teammates recognize your strength, they trust in you. The understanding you have is unmatched.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Trust in yourself, but also trust in the idea that, no matter your teammates, no matter the odds, you can find a way to achieve the goal before you.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: No one person is perfect, but two, or three... when they converge, the power in the center grows, maybe at the cost of some differences and disagreements.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: I'm always pushing you one step further, Fang. Go make yourself into the leader who can guide that power in the center.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Instructor...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: ...Yes. I... I won't give up.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Not everyone can handle the burden of command.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Alright. Believe in yourself. And remember that feeling you had today when you dove in there. You can do it.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Um... But, Instructor Grace... I kinda feel like hearing this stuff from you... it's weird.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ahaha... is it a little different from my usual style?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Not exactly, it's just... a little more... professional? Than usual!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Ah, you know me too well. And I think you can guess who's really telling you this stuff.

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: But even if 'she' isn't here to speak up and tell you herself, she definitely hopes you can get that courage and confidence from somewhere.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Alright! I got it!

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Okay, go rest up. You'll have your first solo temporary duty assignment soon.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huh? So soon?

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: You're not up for it?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Of course I am! I'll be ready...

steps.name: Grace
steps.text: Don't blame me for not reminding you, the first time you make a mistake. And don't cry in front of your team.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I won't! Thank you, Instructor Grace!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (And thank you... Instructor Dobermann.)

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Whew... I almost lost it there. How embarrassing, hehe...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Everyone's encouraging me. And I really do believe I can do it.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Instructor Dobermann, Instructor Grace, I... I think I finally get it. I know what it means to be trusted by your teammates, and how comforting it can be.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I'm... the leader. I have to keep training, and take on more responsibility. That's my decision.
Half an hour later...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Phew... alright.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Team three, up!

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Whew... glad we had some time to rest.

steps.name: Scene
steps.text: Y e s . . .

steps.name: Lens
steps.text: It may have been time to rest, but Captain Fang did not close her eyes. I took many shots of the captain's serious expression as she looked through her combat intelligence.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Erm... it's nothing special...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Phase two begins in twenty minutes. We'll form up for a joint attack with team two, moving in from Area 10, surveying the ground, and taking up a vantage point.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: We're the first to engage the enemy? Not an easy job, but seems right for us.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Captain Fang, what's the plan after that?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I revised my plan based on our previous engagement. Here's your copies to review.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Taking our previous experience into account, I think we'll want to take a more aggressive stance.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Lens and Scene need to stay secure, keep our communications unobstructed. The front line needs clear maps and imaging.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Aciddrop, we still want you on the high ground for covering fire. But don't spread out too much, we want you close.

steps.name: Aciddrop
steps.text: Roger that! My crossbow does more damage at close range.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Frostleaf, you and I will launch an attack on the center of the enemy force. Scout from concealment when you engage.

steps.name: Frostleaf
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Lens's terrain imaging needs to get to team two as quickly as possible. The other team can then move to support us.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Once we break through the first enemy line, we'll direct the supporting fire.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: That's all we've got for the plan before we move. Once we reach Area 10, listen for my orders.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I... appreciate everything you said to me back there. My mistakes in the first phase cost us, we suffered a casualty. I won't make any mistakes again.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: That's the last time I'll misjudge things or give bad orders. Please, trust me.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I now know what it means to be a team leader.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Now, all hands, conduct your equipment checks before we move out.

a.text: Enemy position detected. Prepare for combat!
